title: Fixed-size chunking with overlap
summary: Cut the text every N tokens or characters and step back by an overlap so a sentence near a boundary lands in two chunks. It is the cheapest strategy and the baseline for every other one.
useIf: You need a predictable, cheap baseline, or the text has no headings or paragraphs to split on.
avoidIf: The documents have headings, tables or code. A blind cut will separate rows from headers and bodies from titles.

explain.md: A **fixed-size chunker** slides a window of N units over the text. The window moves forward by `N - overlap`, so neighbouring chunks share `overlap` units. Overlap exists because the cut ignores meaning: a fact that straddles a boundary would otherwise be split in half, and neither half would match the question well.

explain.title: Index inflation from overlap
explain.expr: stored tokens = text tokens x N / (N - overlap)

vars.v: tokens shared with the previous chunk

explain.example: N = 512 and overlap = 128 (25%): 512 / 384 = 1.33, so you embed, store and pay for about 33% more tokens. At 15% overlap the factor is 1.18.

explain.md: Microsoft's chunking guide suggests starting at 512 tokens (about 2,000 characters) with 25% overlap, and also shows a fixed-size example of about 200 words with 10 to 15% overlap [[tr1]]. NVIDIA tested 10, 15 and 20% overlap and found 15% best on one dataset at 1,024 tokens [[tr25]]. Tools differ: Unstructured defaults to `max_characters` 500 and `overlap` 0, which gives small chunks with no safety margin unless you change it [[tr44]].

Choose N from the question type: short facts favour smaller windows and broad questions favour larger ones. Choose overlap from the span of a typical fact: it should at least cover the sentence you cannot afford to cut. Then measure recall on labelled questions at 0, 10 and 20% overlap. That difference is the number that matters, not the guideline.

explain.caption: Text Split skill parameters that matter for fixed-size chunking [[tr2]]
head: Parameter
Value or default
Note
rows: `pages` is the length-capped mode. It tries not to cut a sentence, so chunks can be a little shorter than the maximum
Unit is characters unless you set `unit`
Token mode uses `cl100k_base` by default, and `o200k_base` is not supported

explain.title: Characters are not tokens
explain.md: A rule of thumb is about 4 characters per token for common OpenAI models [[tr1]]. The default 5,000 characters is therefore roughly 1,250 tokens, not 512. If you want 512 tokens, either set about 2,000 characters or switch to token mode and accept that it is preview.

explain.intro: Open the overlap preset: compare 'Fixed 80, no overlap' with 'Add 16 tokens overlap'. Watch where boundaries fall, how many chunks appear and how the total token count grows. Then switch to Recursive and Sentence groups on the same text to see which boundaries each strategy respects.

whereToUse: A first baseline before you spend effort on smarter splitting
Plain text with no structure: transcripts, logs, emails, scraped pages
Very large corpora where ingest cost and simplicity matter more than boundary quality
Pipelines that need stable chunk counts and sizes for capacity planning

use: Text is flat and has no reliable headings
Ingest budget is small and the corpus is large
You need a baseline to beat with measurements
avoid: Documents have headings, tables or code blocks that must stay whole
Citations must map to sections or pages
Questions depend on a clause staying with its heading
flips: Documents arrive with headings: use structure-aware splitting inside sections
Memory or cost is the constraint: lower overlap to 10 to 15% before touching size
Boundary misses dominate failures: raise overlap or move to sentence-aware boundaries

pitfalls.symptom: Chunks are a fraction of the intended size
pitfalls.cause: `maximumPageLength` was set to 512 expecting tokens, but the default unit is characters (about 128 tokens)
pitfalls.fix: Set the unit deliberately, convert with about 4 characters per token, and check real token counts

pitfalls.symptom: Token counts in the index do not match what the chat model sees
pitfalls.cause: Token mode uses `cl100k_base`, and `o200k_base` (used by GPT-4o) is not supported
pitfalls.fix: Leave headroom under limits and measure with the tokenizer of the model you care about

pitfalls.symptom: Two almost identical chunks fill the top results
pitfalls.cause: High overlap means the same sentences live in neighbouring chunks, and both match
pitfalls.fix: Lower overlap, dedupe by document and ordinal position, or return merged neighbours

pitfalls.symptom: Answers that sit across a boundary are still missed
pitfalls.cause: Overlap is smaller than the span of the fact
pitfalls.fix: Check overlap against real question spans, or use sentence-aligned boundaries

scenarios.title: Millions of flat transcripts
scenarios.situation: A nightly batch indexes millions of call transcripts that have no headings. Storage is metered and recall on boundary-spanning facts matters less than coverage.
unknowns: How long is a typical fact span?
scenarios.question: Which chunker do you ship first?

options.name: Fixed 512 tokens with 10 to 15% overlap
options.why: Predictable, cheap and well supported. Overlap covers most boundary cuts at a small inflation.
options.tradeoff: Boundaries ignore topic shifts, so some chunks mix two subjects.

options.name: Semantic splitting on every transcript
options.why: Adds an embedding pass over millions of sentences before the real embedding, for gains studies did not find consistent.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable on a small, high-value corpus after a measured win.

options.name: Recursive splitting with paragraph and sentence separators
options.why: Cleaner boundaries when transcripts have line breaks.
options.tradeoff: Uneven sizes and extra tuning for noisy text.

flips.if: Transcripts carry speaker turns or timestamps
flips.then: Split on turns first, then cap the size.

flips.if: Your labelled questions show boundary misses
flips.then: Raise overlap or add sentence-aligned boundaries.

scenarios.takeaway: At scale on flat text, the cheap baseline is usually the right start.

scenarios.title: Memory cap meets 25% overlap
scenarios.situation: The vector index is close to its memory quota. The pipeline uses 512 token chunks with 25% overlap and the team wants to free space without a rebuild of the embedding model.
scenarios.question: What do you change first?

options.name: Cut overlap to about 10% and re-run the labelled set
options.why: Inflation falls from 1.33 to about 1.11, roughly 17% fewer stored tokens, and the set tells you the recall cost.
options.tradeoff: Boundary-spanning facts become slightly more likely to be missed.

options.name: Keep overlap and quantize the vectors
options.why: Frees much more memory per vector than any overlap change.
options.tradeoff: Needs a new vector field and a reindex, and rescoring settings to tune.

options.name: Remove overlap completely
options.why: Boundary cuts return and cannot be measured away without testing.
options.tradeoff: Fine when chunks are already sentence or paragraph aligned.

flips.if: The corpus is still growing fast
flips.then: Plan quantization now, because overlap tuning buys only a one-off saving.
Keep overlap and fix capacity elsewhere.

scenarios.takeaway: Overlap is a dial with a measurable cost on both memory and recall.

quiz.q: Chunks are 512 tokens with a 128 token overlap. By what percentage do the stored tokens exceed the original text?
quiz.hint: Each new chunk adds N minus overlap new tokens.
quiz.explain: Step = 512 - 128 = 384, so stored tokens = 512 / 384 = 1.333 times the text, which is 33.3% more.

quiz.q: A team sets `maximumPageLength` to 512 in the Text Split skill, expecting 512 token chunks, and leaves `unit` at its default. What do they get?
options: An error, because the minimum is 1,000
quiz.explain: The default unit is characters and the minimum is 300, so 512 is valid and yields about 128 tokens. Token mode needs `unit: azureOpenAITokens`, which is preview. Sentences are set by `textSplitMode`, not by this value.

options: Duplicate hits in the top results
quiz.explain: Overlap means more tokens are embedded and stored, and neighbouring chunks can both match. It does not change vector dimensions or per-vector math.

flashcards.front: What is the index inflation factor for chunk size N and overlap O?
flashcards.back: N / (N - O). With 512 and 128 it is 1.33, so you store about 33% more tokens.

flashcards.front: What are the Text Split skill defaults for page length and overlap?
flashcards.back: `maximumPageLength` 5,000 characters (range 300 to 50,000) and no overlap. The default unit is characters.

flashcards.front: Why can Text Split token counts disagree with GPT-4o token counts?
flashcards.back: Token mode uses `cl100k_base` by default and `o200k_base` is not supported, so counts follow a different tokenizer.
